narrative:
On October 14, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,946 matters across 55 judges and heard 1,164, achieving an overall hearing rate of 39.5%. This marks an 8.3 percentage point recovery from the previous day's 31.2% (928 of 2,979 heard), though it remains below the 45.7% clearance achieved on October 12.

Disposal efficiency varied markedly across individual benches. In Hall 32, Justice G. Basavaraja recorded a strong clearance rate, taking up 59 of 90 scheduled matters (65.6%). Justice H.P. Sandesh (Hall 11) heard 40 of 57 matters (70.2%), while Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar (Hall 22) cleared 86 of 125 matters across two rosters (68.8%). Conversely, notable bottlenecks occurred in Hall 30, where Justice S. Rachaiah heard none of the 148 scheduled matters, and in Hall 31, where Justice C.M. Poonacha took up only 1 of 85 matters on a secondary roster despite hearing 47 of 67 on the primary roster.

By procedural stage, interlocutory matters drove most court business. Orders accounted for the largest volume, converting 430 of 966 scheduled cases (44.5%), up from 37.1% on October 13. Admission stages rebounded significantly, hearing 354 of 780 matters (45.4%) compared to just 26.8% the preceding day. In contrast, Final Hearing matters continued to lag, with only 101 of 499 cases heard (20.2%), reflecting prolonged arguments typical of concluding stages.

Writ Petitions (WP) dominated the docket, representing nearly 45% of total business with 1,326 listings; 462 were heard (34.8%), up from 25.8% yesterday. Criminal matters saw higher velocity: Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) achieved a 45.5% hearing rate (223 of 490), while Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) reached 55.8% (92 of 165). Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) cleared 131 of 368 matters (35.6%), maintaining steady disposal relative to earlier sessions.
